scenes.say: These women glowed in the dark. And it was killing them.
scenes.cap: These women GLOWED in the dark. And it was KILLING them.

scenes.say: In the nineteen-twenties, young women in New Jersey painted watch dials with glowing radium paint.
scenes.cap: In the 1920s, young women in New Jersey painted watch dials with glowing RADIUM paint.

scenes.say: The paint was called Undark. And the bosses taught them one trick.
scenes.cap: The paint was called UNDARK. And the bosses taught them one trick.

scenes.say: Shape the brush with your lips. Dip it in radium. Paint. Hundreds of times a day.
scenes.cap: Shape the brush with your LIPS. Dip it in RADIUM. Paint. Hundreds of times a day.

scenes.say: They were told it was safe. Some even painted their teeth, to glow on a night out.
scenes.cap: They were told it was SAFE. Some even painted their TEETH, to glow on a night out.

scenes.say: Then their teeth fell out. Their jaws began to crumble. Doctors called it radium jaw.
scenes.cap: Then their teeth fell out. Their jaws began to CRUMBLE. Doctors called it RADIUM JAW.

scenes.say: In nineteen twenty-two, Mollie Maggia died. Her death was blamed on syphilis.
scenes.cap: In 1922, Mollie Maggia died. Her death was blamed on SYPHILIS.

scenes.say: Grace Fryer searched for two years to find a lawyer. In nineteen twenty-eight, she and four other women settled with the company.
scenes.cap: Grace Fryer searched for TWO YEARS to find a lawyer. In 1928, she and four other women SETTLED.

scenes.say: Ten years later, Catherine Donohue testified from her deathbed. And won.
scenes.cap: Ten years later, Catherine Donohue testified from her DEATHBED. And WON.

scenes.say: Their fight helped create the worker safety rules that protect people today.
scenes.cap: Their fight helped create the worker SAFETY rules that protect people today.

scenes.say: And radium has a half-life of sixteen hundred years. It is still in their bones.
scenes.cap: And radium has a half-life of 1,600 YEARS. It is still in their BONES.

scenes.say: Follow The Forgotten Lab, for the stories science tried to forget.
scenes.cap: Follow THE FORGOTTEN LAB for the stories science tried to forget.

upload.description:
In the 1920s, the 'Radium Girls' painted glowing watch dials and were taught to point their brushes with their lips. They were told radium was safe. It wasn't.
Their fight in court helped shape the worker-safety rules we have today.

Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radium_Girls
Book: 'The Radium Girls' by Kate Moore
